7. At about 1523 hours, I met Senior Station Officer HUI Kin-on (“SStnO HUI”), who was the initial Incident Commander) at the roundabout near Wang Tai House. He reported to me that firefighting and rescue operations at Wang Cheong House, Wang Tai House and Wang Shing House were in progress and that a Mayday message had been received from a member at about 1522 hours via radiotelephone (“R/T”). SStnO HUI reported that the contents of the message were muffled, the identity of the distressed member(s) could not be verified and confirmed, and the building location was not provided by the distressed member(s). Effort was made by SStnO HUI to clarify the caller’s identity and location via R/T but no response was received from the caller. SStnO HUI formed Emergency Response Teams (“ERTs”) in an attempt to conduct search and rescue operations on 30/F of Wang Cheong House.

8. I instructed SStnO HUI to continue the Mayday operation and report to me of any progress. I also instructed SStnO HUI to continue the firefighting operations at scene. I then conducted an assessment of the vicinity to size up the situation. At about 1525 hours, I noticed that the fire had spread to G/F to about 2/F of the south-west façade of Wang Kin House and to about 4/F of the south façade of Wang Sun House. I instructed crew members to lay 2 hoses for firefighting towards the fire at Wang Kin House and Wang Sun House.
